results.content: Integrating AI techniques into connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and their data fusion, enables a new paradigm that allows for unparalleled real-time awareness of the surrounding environment. The potential of emerging wireless technologies can be fully exploited by establishing communication and cooperation among AI-augmented CAVs and UAVs. However, configuring appropriate deep learning (DL) models for connected vehicles is a complex task. Deep learning (DL) is undoubtedly the primary technology behind many breakthroughs in image recognition, and robotics (Bonsignorio et al. results.title: A systematic mapping and review on machine learning for ...
results.content: ## ICT Express. # A systematic mapping and review on machine learning for non-terrestrial networks assisted Internet of Things: Enabling technologies. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.icte.2026.01.002Get rights and content. Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs), comprising unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), high-altitude platforms (HAPs), and satellites, are increasingly studied as complements to terrestrial infrastructures for extending connectivity to Internet of Things (IoT) devices and sensor networks. To address challenges such as energy constraints, dynamic network conditions, and heterogeneous communication links, a wide range of machine learning (ML) techniques have been explored, including deep learning, reinforcement learning, deep reinforcement learning, and federated learning. This paper addresses this need by presenting a large-scale bibliometric and thematic cluster analysis of ML-based NTN-assisted IoT research with a focus on enabling technologies. The analysis organizes the literature into thematic clusters, examines co-occurrence patterns among enabling technologies and applications, and highlights recurring research directions and emerging topics such as edge intelligence, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, non-orthogonal multiple access, digital twins, and explainable AI.

From Embodied and Physical AI to Autonomous Drone Swarms with Dr. Denis Garagic
Open Data Science and AI Conference
19300 subscribers
1 likes
73 views
17 Dec 2025
In this episode of the ODSC Ai X Podcast, host Sheamus McGovern speaks with Dr. Denis Garagić, CTO at Palladyne AI, about how intelligent systems are moving beyond the screen and into the physical world.
They explore the rise of embodied and physical AI, how it’s transforming robotics and manufacturing, and why autonomous drone swarms represent a powerful shift in real-time, decentralized decision-making. Denis also shares why hybrid models often outperform LLMs in production environments, and what’s needed to safely deploy these systems in industry and defense.

Key Topics Covered

How Denis Garagić’s work connects robotics, AI software, and autonomy.
What Embodied AI and Physical AI mean, and how they differ from traditional automation.
Why embedded, adaptive systems are replacing rigid, pre‑programmed robots in manufacturing.
The role of data, edge compute, and multi‐modal perception in enabling real‑world autonomy.
Internal limitations of large language models (LLMs) in industrial and physical systems, and why hybrid autonomy is often preferable.
How true drone swarms work: decentralized decision‑making, edge planning, and self‑organising UAV fleets.
Use cases in industrial manufacturing (automotive, aerospace, defense, construction) and in public‑safety/drone swarms.
The operational, organisational, and safety challenges of deploying embodied/physical AI in production: workforce readiness, verification & validation, regulatory considerations.
The future of embodied & physical AI: world‑models, runtime memory, sim‑to‑real transfer, and where the industry is headed next.
